title: Knot meets knot only pairwise: failure is invariant exactly under cuts
claim: Knot meets knot only pairwise in the knot's spaces. Let H be a knot's space (a connected cubic system on which not-all-equal fails) with incidence graph B(H). (1) The twist criterion: for a set t of incidences, the signed system H^t (each incidence in t reads its point's colour exchanged) is non-colourable iff t is a cocycle of B(H), an edge set of the form d(S). Switching at S gives one direction. For the other: a connected cubic signed system is non-colourable iff its signed incidence matrix is sign-nonsingular (Seymour's argument with signs), so the plain signing and (-1)^t are both Pfaffian, and the Pfaffian signings of a matching covered bipartite graph form one switching class (THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE A, Lemma 1). (2) If both sides of a nontrivial k-edge cut accept knots (relations passing K1-K3 on the k channels), then k = 2. Such sides are complementary parity cosets (complementarity), so twisting any two cut edges keeps H non-colourable; by (1) every pair of cut edges is a cocycle, so the cut edges lie in series around a cycle of k blobs, and both shores, each holding alternate blobs, are connected only when k = 2. So in the knot's spaces knot meets knot only pairwise (the two-place parity of 2-edge cuts); across three or more channels the parts meet otherwise, a knot against a hub at 3-edge cuts. Checked: the criterion on every twist of every nontrivial 2- and 3-edge cut of ten knot's spaces and on random and random-cocycle incidence sets; the side relations of every nontrivial 2-, 3- and 4-edge cut (4-edge cuts on four small spaces), where both sides accept knots only at 2-edge cuts; controls off the knot's spaces.
failure_conditions: A set of incidences of a knot's space that is not a cocycle but whose twist leaves the space non-colourable, or a cocycle whose twist makes it colourable.
A nontrivial cut of three or more edges of a knot's space whose two sides both accept knots on the channels.
foundation_claim_scope: A structural theorem on the knot's spaces (cubic systems on which not-all-equal fails); no counting claim.

validation.status: checked: the twist criterion on every twist of every nontrivial 2- and 3-edge cut of ten knot's spaces and on random sets and random cocycles; side relations of every nontrivial 2-, 3- and 4-edge cut on the spaces enumerated; controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: Sign-nonsingularity, Pfaffian signings and their uniqueness up to switching are classical (Seymour; Little; Lovasz-Plummer; THREEFOLD-SPACES and THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE record them here); the twist criterion as a statement about the knot's spaces and the pairwise-only theorem are new here.
